tabs.restoreForgotten: It was removed from the saved tabs; if it exists again, open it from “Open repository” or the recent list.

start.title: No repository open
start.hint: Open a repository to see its history.
start.recentEmpty: You haven't opened any repositories yet.

detail.empty: Select a commit to see its details.
detail.author: Author

errors.gitNotFound: Git wasn't found on this computer. Install it (for example with Homebrew or the Xcode Command Line Tools) and reopen GitCRAFT.
errors.pathNotFound: The folder “{{path}}” doesn't exist or is no longer available.
errors.notARepository: The folder “{{path}}” is not a Git repository. Choose the folder of a project that uses Git (or any of its subfolders).
errors.bareRepository: “{{path}}” is a bare repository (it has no working directory). GitCRAFT doesn't support bare repositories yet.
errors.dubiousOwnership: Git refuses to open “{{path}}” because the folder belongs to another user on this system. If you trust it, mark it as safe with “git config --global --add safe.directory” followed by the path.
errors.timedOut: Git took too long to respond. If the repository is on a network drive, check the connection.
errors.unknown: Git returned an unexpected error. Check Git's original output.
errors.identityUnknown: Git doesn't know who you are. Set your name and email with “git config --global user.name "Your Name"” and “git config --global user.email you@example.com”.
errors.nothingToCommit: There are no staged changes to commit.
errors.staleDiff: The file changed since its diff was shown. It has been refreshed: select again what you want.
errors.undoConflict: A file changed since the discard, so nothing was touched. The copy is still in the stash (“GitCRAFT: descarte de …” in git stash list): recover each file with “Recover” on that entry (sidebar → Stashes). Untracked files are in the Trash.
errors.invalidBranchName: That is not a valid branch name.
errors.branchExists: A branch with that name already exists.
errors.branchChanged: The branch changed since it was shown (it was moved, renamed or deleted). Nothing was done; check the sidebar and try again.
errors.branchInWorktree: That branch is in use in another worktree of this repository.
errors.stashChanged: That entry is no longer in the stash (it was applied or deleted elsewhere). Nothing was done.
errors.nothingToStash: There are no uncommitted changes to save.
errors.authFailed: Git could not authenticate with the remote. GitCRAFT never stores or asks for passwords: set up a credential helper (osxkeychain on macOS) or add your SSH key to the agent, and check that “git fetch” works in a terminal.
errors.remoteUnreachable: Could not connect to the remote. Check your connection and the remote's URL (git remote -v).
errors.detachedHead: HEAD is detached (not on a branch): switch to a branch first.

graph.empty: This repository has no commits yet.

optimize.message_one: This repository has {{count}} commit and no Git commit-graph index. Optimizing it makes the history start showing sooner. It only adds an index file: commits, branches and files are not changed.
optimize.message_other: This repository has {{count}} commits and no Git commit-graph index. Optimizing it makes the history start showing sooner. It only adds an index file: commits, branches and files are not changed.
optimize.dismissHint: Don't suggest this again for this repository
optimize.done: Repository optimized. The history will load sooner next time you open it.

files.title: Changed files
files.none: This commit doesn't change any file.

diff.label: Diff of {{path}}
diff.binary: Binary file: its diff can't be shown.
diff.tooLarge_other: This diff has {{count}} lines; showing it all may be slow.
diff.noChanges: There are no text changes in this file.
diff.noNewline: No newline at end of file
diff.selectionHint: Tick lines to stage them on their own (Shift+click for a range).

commit.label: Create commit
commit.summaryTooLong: The summary is longer than the recommended {{limit}} characters; many tools will cut it.
commit.blockedNoSummary: Write a summary for the commit.
commit.publishedTitle: Amend a commit that is already published?
commit.publishedConsequence: Amending creates a new commit that replaces it on your branch. To publish it you will need a force push, and anyone who already fetched it will have to reconcile their history.
commit.publishedRecovery: The original commit is not lost: it remains reachable in the reflog.

discard.title: Discard changes?
discard.tracked_one: The unstaged changes of {{count}} file will be lost (+{{added}} −{{removed}} lines).
discard.tracked_other: The unstaged changes of {{count}} files will be lost (+{{added}} −{{removed}} lines).
discard.lines_one: {{count}} selected line of {{path}} will be discarded (+{{added}} −{{removed}}).
discard.lines_other: {{count}} selected lines of {{path}} will be discarded (+{{added}} −{{removed}}).
discard.untracked_one: {{count}} untracked file will go to the Trash.
discard.untracked_other: {{count}} untracked items will go to the Trash.
discard.backup: A copy is saved in the stash first (“GitCRAFT: descarte de …”) and you can undo it for {{seconds}} seconds.
discard.trashRecovery: Untracked files can be recovered from the Trash.
discard.inStash: A copy is in the stash.

branches.newFromHead: Create a new branch from the current commit
branches.needsCommit: Make the first commit before creating branches
branches.alreadyCurrent: It is already the current branch
branches.checkoutRemote: Switch to a local branch tracking “{{name}}”
branches.cannotDeleteCurrent: The current branch cannot be deleted: switch to another one first
branches.createTracking: Starts at “{{start}}” and tracks it (pull and push go to that remote branch).
branches.name: Name
branches.nameHint: No spaces; slashes are fine, as in “feature/login”.
branches.nameInvalid: That is not a valid branch name (no spaces, no “..”, not starting with “-”…).
branches.renameNote: Only the local name changes: its commits, remote branch and history (reflog) stay.
branches.deleteSafe: No commit is lost: all of them are also on other branches, remote branches or tags.
branches.deleteOrphans_one: This branch has 1 commit that is on no other branch, remote branch or tag. It would be left without a branch:
branches.deleteOrphans_other: This branch has {{count}} commits that are on no other branch, remote branch or tag. They would be left without a branch:
branches.upstreamKept: The remote branch “{{upstream}}” is not deleted.
branches.recreate: To create it again as it is now:
branches.blocked_one: You have uncommitted changes in 1 file that is different on “{{name}}”, and Git does not overwrite it:
branches.blocked_other: You have uncommitted changes in {{count}} files that are different on “{{name}}”, and Git does not overwrite them:
branches.notForced: Nothing was touched: you are still on the current branch with your changes.
branches.stashExplained_one: You can save your uncommitted changes (1 file) in the stash and switch. They are kept as “GitCRAFT: antes de cambiar a {{name}}” and never deleted automatically.
branches.stashExplained_other: You can save all your uncommitted changes ({{count}} files) in the stash and switch. They are kept as “GitCRAFT: antes de cambiar a {{name}}” and never deleted automatically.
branches.stashed: Switched to “{{name}}”. Your previous changes are in the stash as “GitCRAFT: antes de cambiar a {{name}}”.
branches.deleted: Branch “{{name}}” deleted. To create it again:
branches.failed: The branch operation could not be completed.
branches.failedAfterStash: If they were saved, your changes are in the stash as “GitCRAFT: antes de cambiar a {{name}}” (git stash list).

stash.needsCommit: Make the first commit before using the stash
stash.createHint: Save your uncommitted changes in the stash
stash.noChanges: There are no uncommitted changes to save
stash.createExplained: Your uncommitted changes are saved in a new stash entry and the working directory goes back to the last commit. You can apply them later.
stash.messageHint: Without a message, Git names it after the last commit.
stash.nothingToSave: Nothing to save with these options.
stash.blocked_one: The entry changes 1 file where you have uncommitted changes (or that already exists), and Git does not overwrite it:
stash.blocked_other: The entry changes {{count}} files where you have uncommitted changes (or that already exist), and Git does not overwrite them:
stash.saveLocalExplained: Alternative: first save your current changes in the stash (as “GitCRAFT: antes de aplicar …”, never deleted) and then apply. Or cancel, commit or discard your changes, and try again.
stash.conflicts_one: 1 file also changed on the current branch since the entry was made and would conflict:
stash.conflicts_other: {{count}} files also changed on the current branch since the entry was made and would conflict:
stash.mayConflict_one: 1 file also changed on the current branch since the entry was made and might conflict:
stash.mayConflict_other: {{count}} files also changed on the current branch since the entry was made and might conflict:
stash.conflictExplained: If you apply anyway, those files get conflict markers (<<<<<<< … >>>>>>>) for you to resolve by hand. The entry is not deleted. Alternative: cancel and apply it on the branch it was made on.
stash.popKeeps: Although you asked for “pop”, the entry will not be deleted because there will be conflicts.
stash.dropLoses: The changes saved in it are lost, unless you recover it before Git cleans up loose objects (usually weeks).
stash.dropLosesUntracked: The changes saved in it, including its untracked files, are lost unless you recover it before Git cleans up loose objects (usually weeks).
stash.failed: The stash operation could not be completed.
stash.applied: Entry applied. It is still in the stash.
stash.popped: Entry applied and deleted from the stash.
stash.localSaved: Your previous changes are in the stash as “GitCRAFT: antes de aplicar …”.
stash.conflicted_one: Entry applied with conflicts in 1 file; resolve and stage it. The entry is still in the stash.
stash.conflicted_other: Entry applied with conflicts in {{count}} files; resolve and stage them. The entry is still in the stash.
stash.gone: This entry is no longer in the stash.

originLong.discard: Backup GitCRAFT saved before discarding changes.
originLong.beforeSwitch: Changes GitCRAFT saved before switching branches.

stash.recoverHint: “Recover” puts a file back as it was right before the discard, without touching staged changes.
stash.recoverLoses_one: You changed this file since the discard. Recovering replaces its current content, and this line, which the copy does not have, would be lost:
stash.recoverLoses_other: You changed this file since the discard. Recovering replaces its current content, and these {{count}} lines, which the copy does not have, would be lost:
stash.recoverWhole: This file cannot be compared line by line (it is binary or no longer tracked). Recovering replaces its current content entirely.
stash.recoverKeeps: Only the file in the working directory changes: staged changes are not touched and the entry stays in the stash.
stash.recovered: “{{path}}” recovered as it was before the discard. The entry is still in the stash.
stash.alreadyRecovered: “{{path}}” already has the saved content: nothing to recover.

remote.busy: A remote operation is already running
remote.fetchHint: Download new commits and branches from every remote (your branches and files do not change)
remote.fetchAllPrune: Fetch all and remove deleted remote branches (--prune)
remote.fetchOnePrune: Fetch “{{remote}}” and remove its deleted branches (--prune)
remote.fetched: Fetched {{remote}}. Your branches and files did not change.
remote.pullNeedsBranch: Switch to a branch to pull

pullHint.merge: Bring the upstream's new commits in with a merge
pullHint.rebase: Bring the upstream's new commits in with a rebase

tracking.gone: It tracked “{{upstream}}”, which no longer exists on the remote
tracking.detached: Detached HEAD: you are not on any branch

blocked.overwrite_one: The incoming commits change 1 file where you have uncommitted changes (or that already exists untracked), and Git does not overwrite it:
blocked.overwrite_other: The incoming commits change {{count}} files where you have uncommitted changes (or that already exist untracked), and Git does not overwrite them:
blocked.rebaseNeedsClean_one: A pull with rebase needs no uncommitted changes in tracked files, and you have 1:
blocked.rebaseNeedsClean_other: A pull with rebase needs no uncommitted changes in tracked files, and you have {{count}}:

pull.unresolved: A merge or rebase is waiting on conflicts. Resolve or abort it (banner above) before pulling again.

alternatives.overwrite: Alternative: first save your changes in the stash (as “GitCRAFT: antes de hacer pull”, never deleted) and pull. You can apply them later from the sidebar. Or cancel and commit or discard your changes.
alternatives.rebaseNeedsClean: Alternatives: first save your changes in the stash (as “GitCRAFT: antes de hacer pull”, never deleted) and pull; or cancel and switch the strategy to merge (Pull's ▾ menu), which only stops if the changes clash.

pull.conflicts_one: 1 file changed both on your branch and on “{{upstream}}” and would conflict:
pull.conflicts_other: {{count}} files changed both on your branch and on “{{upstream}}” and would conflict:
pull.mayConflict_one: 1 file changed both on your branch and on “{{upstream}}” and might conflict:
pull.mayConflict_other: {{count}} files changed both on your branch and on “{{upstream}}” and might conflict:

conflictExplained.merge: If you go on, the merge stops with conflict markers (<<<<<<< … >>>>>>>) in those files: resolve them in your editor, stage them and commit. You can abort it at any time and go back to how things are now.
conflictExplained.rebase: If you go on, the rebase stops at the first commit that clashes: resolve the files, stage them and continue with “git rebase --continue” in a terminal. You can abort it at any time and go back to how things are now.

pull.abortExplained: The branch goes back to how it was before it started, and any conflict resolutions made since are lost. Uncommitted changes you had before in other files are kept.
pull.inProgressConflicts_one: 1 file still has conflicts: resolve it in your editor and stage it.
pull.inProgressConflicts_other: {{count}} files still have conflicts: resolve them in your editor and stage them.

inProgressNext.merge: No conflicts left: commit to finish it.
inProgressNext.rebase: No conflicts left: continue with “git rebase --continue” in a terminal.
inProgressNext.cherryPick: No conflicts left: commit to finish it.
inProgressNext.revert: No conflicts left: commit to finish it.

how.rebase: (your commits replayed on top with rebase).

pull.noUpstream: Branch “{{branch}}” has no upstream, so there is nowhere to pull from. Publish it with Push to create one.
pull.upstreamGone: “{{upstream}}” no longer exists on the remote (it was deleted there). There is nowhere to pull from.

conflicted.merge_one: The merge stopped with conflicts in 1 file:
conflicted.merge_other: The merge stopped with conflicts in {{count}} files:
conflicted.rebase_one: The rebase stopped with conflicts in 1 file:
conflicted.rebase_other: The rebase stopped with conflicts in {{count}} files:

aborted.merge: Merge aborted: everything is as before the pull.
aborted.rebase: Rebase aborted: everything is as before the pull.

pull.savedLocal: Your previous changes are in the stash as “GitCRAFT: antes de hacer pull”; apply them from the sidebar whenever you want.

push.needsBranch: Switch to a branch to push
push.hint: Upload this branch's commits to its upstream
push.noUpstream: Branch “{{branch}}” has no upstream: it is not published on any remote yet.
push.publishExplained: “{{remote}}/{{branch}}” will be created and become its upstream, so later pulls and pushes go there.

rejectedTitle.stale: The remote changed since it was checked

rejected.remoteAhead: “{{upstream}}” has commits your branch does not. Pull first to bring them in, then push again.
rejected.stale: Someone pushed to “{{upstream}}” after the confirmation was shown, so the force push was not done. Try again to see what it would overwrite now.
rejected.remote: The server rejected the push to “{{upstream}}” (for example a protected branch or a hook). Its answer:
rejected.other: Git rejected the push to “{{upstream}}”. Its answer:

push.forceHint: If you really want to replace those commits, use “Force push (with lease)…” in Push's ▾ menu: it shows first which ones would be lost.
push.forceNotNeeded: “{{upstream}}” has no commits your branch lacks: a normal push is enough and overwrites nothing.
push.forceOverwrites_one: 1 remote commit your branch does not have would be overwritten. It would disappear from “{{upstream}}” for everyone using it:
push.forceOverwrites_other: {{count}} remote commits your branch does not have would be overwritten. They would disappear from “{{upstream}}” for everyone using it:
push.forceLease: Uses --force-with-lease: if someone pushes anything else before it happens (the remote is no longer at {{sha}}), the push is rejected and nothing is lost.
push.forceRecover: While you have the remote branch downloaded, you can keep them in a branch with:
push.forced_one: Force push done: “{{upstream}}” now points to your branch (1 commit uploaded).
push.forced_other: Force push done: “{{upstream}}” now points to your branch ({{count}} commits uploaded).
push.published: Branch published to “{{upstream}}”, now its upstream.
push.upToDate: Nothing to push: “{{upstream}}” already has all your commits.
